notes.summary: All-support characteristic coefficients realize fibrewise maximum as one actual primary profile.
notes.detailedSummary: For an excellent NORMAL local DOMAIN and a finite DOMAIN cover with all centres, arbitrary characteristic and all prime supports, proves the least-root/characteristic-coefficient identity including inseparable multiplicities. Exact primary-power truncation removes nonprimary/zero coefficient ideals. Rational profiles map to one rational primary profile; uniform density and finite-fibre decreasing nets give geometric C/D maximum operators without group actions or flatness.
notes.text:
\section{n1. Characteristic coefficients realize the full fibre maximum}
\textit{Support: ENTIRE qualified G331. This section is new scoped mathematics.}

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent NORMAL local domain of positive
dimension and let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be a finite domain extension.
Keep ALL closed centres of the semilocal $S$. Fix a proper primary
$\mathfrak a\subset R$, set $X=V_{\mathfrak a}(R)$,
$Y=V_{\mathfrak aS}(S)$, and let $\rho:Y\to X$ be restriction.
Every prime support is retained. The classes $C,D$ are exactly G331's
independently geometric classes: actual negative effective finite REAL
Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, with degree
at least zero on EVERY contracted proper integral curve before comparison
or limits; their proved uniform and actual decreasing-net completions.
All source, model, historical-audit and literal radial qualifications of
the ENTIRE grant remain in force. No envelope theorem is imported.

We use the following precise result proved in G331 n3. Put
$K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}S$, $n=[L:K]$.
Choose a finite field $M/K$ containing every embedding image of $L$, and
its finite integral closure $E$ of $R$. For any $v\in X$ lift $v$ to
a semivaluation $\widetilde v$ of $E$. There are embeddings
$\sigma:L\hookrightarrow M$ and a common inseparable length $q$,
$q|\Sigma|=n$, such that
\[
 \mu_v=q\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\delta_{w_\sigma},\qquad
 w_\sigma(s)=\widetilde v(\sigma s),
 \qquad \operatorname{supp}\mu_v=\rho^{-1}(v).
\]
The measure is lift-independent, and has mass $n$. In particular EVERY
fibre is nonempty and finite of size at most $n$, including nonminimal
supports and all marked centres. This is a granted full-support theorem,
not a generic-support transitivity or defectlessness assumption.

Let $J\subset S$ be any ideal containing $\mathfrak a^N S$ for some
integer $N\ge1$; it may be unit at some or all centres. Choose finite
R-MODULE generators $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $J$. For
$b(T)=\sum_iT_ib_i$ form the characteristic polynomial of multiplication
by $b(T)$ on the $n$-dimensional $K(T)$-space $L(T)$:
\[
 \chi_J(Z,T)=Z^n+\sum_{l=1}^n(-1)^l c_l(T)Z^{n-l}
           =\prod_{\sigma\in\Sigma}(Z-\sigma b(T))^q.
\]
Here $c_l\in R[T]$. Indeed the determinant first places them in $K[T]$.
The factorization places each coefficient in the integral closure of $R$
in $M$, as an elementary symmetric polynomial in integral elements.
Normality $R=K\cap E$ then places it in $R$. The factorization is valid
also inseparably: over an algebraic closure the field algebra decomposes
into factors of common length $q$, and the determinant on each factor
is its residue scalar to that length, as proved in G331 n3.
Let $I_l(J)$ be the ideal of coefficients of $c_l(T)$, permitting zero.
Generator changes are linear substitutions over $R$; substituting in
both directions proves independence of every $I_l$ from the R-module
generating set. No primary assertion is made for the $I_l$.

We prove, on EVERY support,
\[
 s_J(v):=\min_{\rho w=v}w(J)
       =\min_{1\le l\le n}\frac{v(I_l(J))}{l}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Kill the support $P$ of $\widetilde v$ FIRST, and work in the valued
quotient field $\operatorname{Frac}(E/P)$, then in its rational function
field in the independent variables $T$. Its Gauss valuation is minimum
coefficient value. Multiplicativity follows by dividing each polynomial
by a coefficient of least finite value and reducing to a nonzero residue
polynomial; the product of two such polynomials is nonzero. This also
constructs the extension to rational functions by subtraction of finite
polynomial values. We have not extended a nonzero-support semivaluation
to $\operatorname{Frac}R$ or $\operatorname{Frac}S$.

The $n$ labelled roots in this valued field are the linear polynomials
$\sigma b(T)$, each repeated $q$ times. Their values are $w_\sigma(J)$:
R-module generation and nonnegative values of R-coefficients justify the
minimum over $b_i$. All are finite since $J$ contains a boundary power.
Let $s$ be their least value and $k$ the number, WITH multiplicities,
having value $s$. Every term of $c_l$ has value at least $ls$.
In $c_k$ exactly ONE labelled subset consists of all the $k$ least-valued
roots. Its product has value $ks$; every other subset includes a root
of larger value and has value strictly greater than $ks$.
The ultrametric inequality, applied also after moving this unique term
to the other side, makes the value of $c_k$ exactly $ks$.
Thus the minimum on the right of (1) is $s$.
Full support of the GRANTED positive measure identifies $s$ with the
minimum over the ENTIRE actual fibre. Repeated inseparable roots are
labelled here; even if intermediate coefficients vanish in characteristic
$p$, the unique least subset for this particular $k$ survives. No Newton
polygon citation or no-cancellation assumption is used.

The obstruction that $I_l$ need not be primary is removed EXACTLY.
Define actual downstairs ideals
\[
 K_l=I_l(J)+\mathfrak a^{lN},\qquad
 D_n=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n),\qquad
 B_{J,N}=\sum_{l=1}^n K_l^{D_n/l}.
\]
Every $K_l$ and $B_{J,N}$ is unit-or-primary. The latter contains
$\mathfrak a^{D_nN}$. Since $0\le s_J\le N$, (1) gives
\[
 \frac{v(B_{J,N})}{D_n}
 =\min_l\frac{v(K_l)}l
 =\min_l\min\left(\frac{v(I_l)}l,N\right)=s_J(v).             \tag{2}
\]
This includes zero coefficient ideals, unit centres and every infinite
element value. The truncation does not merely approximate the maximum:
it preserves it exactly. Different allowed cutoffs give the same profile;
equality of the resulting ideals is not claimed.

Consequently for EVERY rational source profile $u=-w(J)/r$, $r\ge1$,
\[
 \mathcal M_\rho u(v):=\max_{\rho w=v}u(w)
             =-\frac{v(B_{J,N})}{D_n r}.                    \tag{3}
\]
The right side has actual geometric positivity BEFORE limits: on the
ACTUAL primary blowup of $B_{J,N}$ its divisor $-E/(D_nr)$ is negative
effective and relatively ample, so has positive degree on every contracted
proper integral curve. Units give zero. Equivalently (2) is the finite
maximum of actual primary profiles. Nothing is inferred from Weil
coefficients on a nonnormal unavailable model.

G331 supplies rational-profile uniform density also on the semilocal
source (Artinian boundary-quotient gluing). Fibre maximum is 1-Lipschitz
on bounded functions. Applying (3) to rational approximants therefore
proves $\mathcal M_\rho:C_S\to C_R$, with finite continuous values.
If $u=\inf_i u_i\in D_S$ is an ACTUAL decreasing C-net, then
\[
 \max_{\rho w=v}\inf_i u_i(w)
       =\inf_i\max_{\rho w=v}u_i(w).                         \tag{4}
\]
For a finite fibre and any finite $t$ exceeding its maximum limit, each
point eventually has value below $t$; directedness supplies one common
index. This proves the nontrivial inequality, also when the maximum
limit is $-\infty$. Thus $\mathcal M_\rho u$ is represented by the
ACTUAL decreasing net $\mathcal M_\rho u_i$ in $C_R$ and belongs to $D_R$.
There is no nested-net flattening or increasing-limit assumption.

For either class, $\mathcal M_\rho\rho^*=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\rho^*\mathcal M_\rho u\ge u$. Moreover
\[
 \mathcal M_\rho u\le g\ \Longleftrightarrow\ u\le\rho^*g.
\]
Hence $\rho^*\mathcal M_\rho$ is the least fibre-constant geometric
majorant within that class. It preserves finite maxima and positive
scaling; it is subadditive, with no asserted additive trace identity.
In a finite tower of normal domains these maximum operators compose,
because the full fibres are unions of the next-stage full fibres.

Under a primary change $d(v)=v(\mathfrak b)>0$, every lift has denominator
$w(\mathfrak bS)=d(v)$, so (1)--(4) and maximum transport divide by the
same positive factor. G331 completion transports the full boundaries and
these class operators; no equivalence of arbitrary model categories or
coefficient-ideal base-change identity is asserted. If R has dimension
zero all sections are empty and there is just the unique empty operator.
There are no empty fibres in positive dimension under this finite injection.

notes.summary: Normal finite-cover raw envelopes commute exactly; known source continuity and model rates transfer.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves raw C/D envelope pullback and full-fibre constancy for every finite continuous signed pulled obstacle, without CE assumptions. A continuous-envelope source implies target continuous greatest C/D envelopes. Canonical ideals contract exactly, every degree converges uniformly when envelopes exist, and an actually established all-support source K0/m bound yields target n(K0+M1)/l in every degree. No extension equality, universal cover existence, arbitrary rate or FG assertion.
notes.text:
\section{n2. Exact envelope transfer and every-degree approximation}
\textit{Supports: ENTIRE qualified G331; own n1.}

Use exactly n1's normal-target finite-domain inclusion, all source centres,
all supports and extended-primary gauges. No group action, flatness,
Galois transitivity, residue perfection, CM or Q-Gorenstein hypothesis is
imposed. For every finite continuous signed obstacle $f$ on $X$, put
$F=\rho^*f$. The raw geometric suprema satisfy the NEW identity
\[
                 \rho^*p_R(f)=p_S(F).                      \tag{5}
\]
This identity holds even if neither raw supremum is an envelope member.
In particular the source raw supremum of a pulled obstacle is constant
on EVERY full fibre. Continuity is not assumed to obtain this constancy.

We first reconstruct the canonical facts needed for the word envelope;
these are foundations, not novelty. On either nonempty compact section
set $B=\max(0,-\min f)$ and
\[
 A_m(f)=\{b:v(b)+mf(v)\ge0\text{ at EVERY point}\},\quad
 A_0=R,\quad h_m=-v(A_m)/m.
\]
For semilocal S the same tests use all its marked sections. These are
ideals containing $\mathfrak a^{\lceil mB\rceil}$, and
$A_mA_l\subset A_{m+l}$. They are unit-or-primary on R and boundary
ideals on S, with unit components allowed. A monic ideal-integrality
equation for $b$ violating one finite threshold would have its leading
term uniquely least-valued: its degree-i coefficient has value at least
$i(-mf(v))$. Thus the ideals are integrally closed, including all
infinite-value supports. Every $h_m$ is finite continuous, below $f$,
and actually negative effective ample on its own primary blowup BEFORE
limits. The unit case is zero.

Rational-profile density in G331 gives
\[
 p_C(f)=p_D(f)=\sup_m h_m,
 \qquad -B\le p_C(f)\le\min(f,0).                          \tag{6}
\]
For a C competitor choose a close rational profile and subtract a small
negative rational boundary constant; powers and a common denominator
give a rational profile below $f$. If $-v(I)/r\le f$ then
$I\subset A_r$. Arbitrarily small errors establish the C equality.
For a D competitor $g=\inf_i g_i\le f$, the increasing directed open
sets $\{g_i<f+\epsilon\}$ cover the compact section. A finite subcover
and directedness choose one index everywhere, and $g_i-\epsilon\in C$
is below $f$ and at least $g-\epsilon$. This proves the D equality,
including partial bottom. Constants $-B$ are boundary-ideal profiles.

Let $M_1=\|v(A_1)\|_\infty$ and $H_N=\max_{r\le N}h_r$.
For $m=kr+s$, $0\le s<r$, grading and nonpositivity imply
\[
 h_m\ge (kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m\ge h_r-rM_1/m,
 \qquad H_N-NM_1/m\le h_m\le p_C(f).
\]
Therefore EVERY degree converges pointwise to the finite LSC raw
supremum. If that supremum is continuous, compactness of the strict-test
cover $\{H_N>p_C-\epsilon\}$ yields uniform convergence of every $h_m$.
Conversely uniform convergence places it in C. A greatest D minorant
equals the raw supremum, so is USC as a decreasing completion, hence
continuous as well. Greatest C existence, greatest D existence, raw
continuity and uniform canonical convergence are consequently equivalent.
Negative constant shifts of competitors prove the obstacle map is
1-Lipschitz. No finite-generation premise or counterexample from
non-finite-generation is used.

To prove (5), pulling a target competitor up gives one inequality.
For every source C competitor $u\le F$, n1 gives an ACTUAL geometric
target competitor $\mathcal M_\rho u\in C_R$ with
$\mathcal M_\rho u\le f$ and $u\le\rho^*\mathcal M_\rho u$.
Taking suprema gives the reverse inequality. Equation (6) makes it
equally an identity for the raw D suprema. This proof uses the newly
proved positive maximum operator, not a declaration that a fibre extremum
is psh. It also proves the greatest-envelope equivalence for this fixed
obstacle on target and on its pullback source: (5), the compact quotient,
and (6) show continuity on one side iff on the other.

In particular suppose S has continuous geometric envelopes for every
finite continuous obstacle on its full boundary. Then R has the same
property, and
\[
      P_R f\in C_R,\qquad \rho^*P_R f=P_S(\rho^*f).          \tag{7}
\]
It dominates ALL target D competitors. Its canonical primary profiles
converge uniformly in EVERY degree and have actual curve-degree
positivity before convergence. The hypothesis can be weakened to source
continuity just for this pulled obstacle. This is a complete conditional
finite-cover theorem, not an assertion that every normal germ has such
a cover or that every regular source in positive/mixed characteristic
has the required continuity.

There is exact canonical contraction, with no extension equality:
\[
           A_m^R(f)=A_m^S(F)\cap R.                        \tag{8}
\]
Indeed every source value on an R element is its restricted value, and
restriction is surjective on the full sections. In completion the same
identity transports through G331's exact primary contraction and
boundary homeomorphisms, without a claim of unchanged generic degree or
of coefficient ideals commuting with every base change.

We prove a useful every-degree quantitative transfer. Let
$J_m=A_m^S(F)$ and $H=P_SF=\rho^*P_Rf$. Suppose a finite $K_0\ge0$
has actually been established such that
\[
        0\le H-h_m^S\le K_0/m \quad\text{on ALL of }Y.      \tag{9}
\]
Set $\mathcal N(J_m)=I_n(J_m)$, the last coefficient ideal in n1.
This is unit-or-primary without truncation: add generators $x$ of a
boundary power inside $J_m$ as redundant module generators; the pure
coefficient $x^n$ belongs to $I_n$. Its radical is therefore maximal
in the proper case. Product Gauss multiplicativity, on the SUPPORT
QUOTIENT field used in n1, gives
\[
 v(\mathcal N(J_m))=q\sum_{\sigma}w_\sigma(J_m),\qquad
 \kappa_m(v):=-v(\mathcal N(J_m))/(nm)
             ={1\over n}\int h_m^S\,d\mu_v.
\]
This is a primary profile with actual ample positivity. EVERY summand
is at most $f(v)$, so every coefficient obeys the canonical test and
$\mathcal N(J_m)\subset A_{nm}^R(f)$. Every summand is at least
$P_Rf(v)-K_0/m$, by (9) and (7). Hence
\[
        h_{nm}^R\ge\kappa_m\ge P_Rf-K_0/m.                 \tag{10}
\]
Generic inseparable lengths give the mass $n$; no ramification/residue
degree equality, flat determinant norm or equal source profiles on each
fibre is assumed. The profiles $h_m^S$ themselves need not be fibre
constant.

For $l=nm+s$, $0\le s<n$, $m\ge1$, target grading gives
\[
 h_l^R\ge (nm/l)h_{nm}^R-sM_1/l
       \ge P_Rf-(nK_0+sM_1)/l.
\]
The missing fraction of $P_Rf\le0$ only improves this bound.
For $1\le l<n$, $A_1^l\subset A_l$ gives $h_l\ge-M_1$.
Thus the single bound, on EVERY support and in EVERY degree, is
\[
           0\le P_Rf-h_l^R\le {n(K_0+M_1)\over l}.         \tag{11}
\]
For $f\ge0$ all canonical ideals are units and errors are zero.
For arbitrary continuous obstacles we claim uniform convergence, not
the existence of (9), a rational envelope, finite generation, or a rate.

There is also an exact maximum-based inclusion. Take
$N\ge\max(1,\lceil mB\rceil)$ in n1. Each
$I_l(J_m)+\mathfrak a^{lN}$ obeys the degree-$lm$ canonical tests,
by the root-value lower bound. Consequently
\[
 B_{J_m,N}\subset A_{D_nm}^R(f),\qquad
 h_{D_nm}^R\ge\mathcal M_\rho h_m^S.
\]
The norm construction is what keeps (11) at generic degree $n$.

For a decreasing net of finite continuous obstacles $f_i$ on a target
with this continuity property, $\inf_iP_Rf_i$ is an ACTUAL D member
and the greatest D minorant of $\inf_i f_i$. It is below the limit;
every competitor below that limit is below every $P_Rf_i$. Equation
(7) commutes with these decreasing nets and includes the bottom limit.
Gauge changes divide obstacles, profiles, raw and attained envelopes
by the same positive fibre denominator; the homogeneous cocycle is
G331's exact one. Dimension zero is the unique empty envelope. Products,
energy and unrestricted finite operators are separate targets.

notes.text:
\section{n3. Full normalization compatibility with finite-covered normal sources}
\textit{Supports: ENTIRE qualified G331; own n1; own n2.}

Here R is any positive-dimensional excellent REDUCED local ring, not
necessarily a domain or equidimensional. Let S be its finite normalization,
keep every marked normal local centre, and let
$\mathfrak c=(R:S)\subset R$. G331 gives a regular conductor element,
the full compact quotient $\rho:Y\to X$, singleton fibres on
$X^\circ=\{v:v(\mathfrak c)<\infty\}$, and precisely conductor-quotient
fibres at infinite value. All nonminimal supports are kept. Let
$Y^\circ=\rho^{-1}X^\circ$. The underlying domain-localization argument
and fibre-gap argument of supplied 429 are reconstructed below, not
credited as new results. The extension to reduced targets and normal
normalization centres with the finite-cover continuity of n2 is the
new scope in this note.

We explicitly use a result of the ENTIRE supplied grant, not a fresh
density source application: G331 n6 proves that support-zero divisorial
valuations are dense on the full section of every positive-dimensional
excellent local domain. Its Rees-DVR/birational argument and the precise
published dependencies remain qualified as in its ledger. A regular
conductor element is nonzero on each normalization domain centre and has
finite value at every such divisorial point. Therefore $Y^\circ$ is dense
in Y, by applying that GRANTED theorem on each clopen centre. This is
not a density inference merely from the word normal, nor a new density
proof or new source-reading credit. The same conclusion in the smooth
closed domain also follows from the supplied translated-Gauss argument,
which is retained as DATA but is not needed as an additional premise.

For finite continuous signed $f$ on X and $F=\rho^*f$, the canonical
lemma reconstructed in n2 applies without target normality: it uses only
G331 comparison, compactness, rational primary density and grading. Thus
both raw C/D suprema on each ring equal the canonical suprema.
Pulling target competitors up always gives
\[
                 \rho^*p_R(f)\le p_S(F)\quad\text{on Y}.    \tag{12}
\]
On EVERY finite-conductor point there is equality, without source
continuity. Indeed let $J=A_m^S(F)$, $q=-w(J)/m\le F$ and choose an
integer $M\ge\max(1,\|q\|_\infty,\max(0,-\min f))$.
For every integer $r\ge1$ the actual downstairs ideal
\[
              B_r=\mathfrak c J^r+\mathfrak a^{mrM}\subset R
\]
is finitely generated, unit-or-primary. The containment uses that the
conductor is an S-ideal contained in R, including every component of S.
Its extended S-ideal is exactly the displayed sum. Consequently, using
only finite ideal generators and their nonnegative coefficients,
\[
 -w(B_r)/(mr)
       =\max\{q(w)-w(\mathfrak c)/(mr),-M\}\le F(w).        \tag{13}
\]
This includes $w(\mathfrak c)=\infty$, where only the truncated term
survives, and involves no subtraction of two infinities. Surjectivity
makes it a target minorant. The proper case has actual negative effective
ample Cartier presentation on its ACTUAL primary blowup and positive
degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. At a finite-conductor point
(13) tends to $q(w)$. Supremizing over m proves equality in (12) on
$Y^\circ$. No uniform conductor error, generic-support deletion or psh
status for a raw increasing supremum is asserted.

Suppose now that $H=p_S(F)$ is continuous. Then the exact criterion is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{a greatest target C or D minorant exists}\quad\Longleftrightarrow
 \quad H\text{ is constant on EVERY full fibre of }\rho.     \tag{14}
 \end{gathered}
\]
If fibre-constant, H is in $C_S$ by the canonical continuity criterion.
G331 full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives $h\in C_R$ with $\rho^*h=H$.
It is below f and dominates every target competitor by (12).
Conversely a greatest target minorant is continuous by n2's canonical
criterion. Its pullback equals H on the dense $Y^\circ$ by (13), hence
everywhere by continuity. That proves full-fibre constancy. The quotient
identification and positive descent used here are the full G331 results,
including infinite-conductor supports, not just topological descent.

If two lifts of v have $H(w_+)-H(w_-)=\Delta>0$, choose a net
$w_i\in Y^\circ$ tending to $w_+$. Its restrictions $v_i$ tend to v,
and (12)--(13) imply
\[
 p_R(f)(v)\le H(w_-),\qquad p_R(f)(v_i)\longrightarrow H(w_+).
\]
Thus the raw supremum has a non-USC jump at least $\Delta$.
Every actual D minorant g is USC and satisfies
$\limsup_i g(v_i)\le g(v)\le H(w_-)$, also when g(v) is bottom.
Therefore
\[
       \sup_X(p_R(f)-g)\ge\Delta,
       \qquad \|p_R(f)-h_m^R\|_\infty\ge\Delta
       \quad\text{for EVERY degree }m.                     \tag{15}
\]
This also excludes finite generation of the canonical algebra: finitely
many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$ give a profile
$-\min_j v(b_j)/d_j=-v((b_j^{D/d_j}))/D$ for common multiple D.
Their degree-one generators generate $A_1$, which contains a boundary
power, so that displayed ideal is unit-or-primary. Its continuous profile
would be the raw supremum, contradicting (15). Failure of finite
generation by itself has not been used to infer discontinuity.
If source continuity is known for all pulled obstacles, a uniform
perturbation of size $\epsilon<\Delta/2$ leaves a gap at least
$\Delta-2\epsilon$, by the Lipschitz bound for the source raw supremum.

The NEW finite-cover application of (14) is the following. For every
normalization centre $S_i$, suppose there is an actual finite domain
extension $S_i\hookrightarrow T_i$, retaining all its closed centres,
such that $T_i$ has continuous geometric envelopes for finite continuous
obstacles. Own n2 then proves source continuity on $S_i$ without a group
action or flatness. The finite product of these local envelopes is H on S:
G331's semilocal gluing identifies C and D with their centre products.
Thus (14) holds for EVERY continuous signed obstacle on the reduced R,
with arbitrary full conductor geometry and these covered normal centres.
The entire criterion is obstacle-specific. We do not prove that every
nonsingleton normalization fibre supplies an obstacle with a discrepancy,
or give an intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient ring classification.

Primary changes divide H and every fibre gap by
$d(v)=v(\mathfrak b)>0$, which is constant on the full fibre;
the gap at v becomes $\Delta/d(v)$. Completion uses the exact G331
boundary and primary-ideal transport, including reductions of any
completed nilpotents. Normal R has unit conductor and singleton
normalization fibres; this criterion then reduces to its source
continuity hypothesis. Zero-dimensional reductions are empty and direct.
The min(f,0) reduced-curve comparison and literal radial distinction are
recorded in n4, not replaced by this conductor criterion.

notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs source CE and signed-model K0/m from six fully read immediate BFJ units only for smooth AFFINE CLOSED algebraically closed CHARACTERISTIC-ZERO germs and their completions. Applies new transfer to actual finite covers of normal targets without group-action or flatness assumptions, and to normalization centres. Preserves geometric curve min(f,0), full gauges/supports/completion, unit/bottom/empty cases, and the distinct literal radial class. General normal CE and higher-characteristic sources remain open.
notes.text:
\section{n4. Source-qualified normal regular covers, gauges and curve comparison}
\textit{Supports: ENTIRE qualified G331; own n1; own n2; own n3.}

Here is a complete scoped consequence beyond finite invariant inclusions.
Let R be an excellent NORMAL local domain, $R\hookrightarrow S$ finite
with S a domain, and keep all marked closed centres of S. Suppose each
local source centre is a smooth AFFINE CLOSED germ over an algebraically
closed field of CHARACTERISTIC ZERO, or its completion with formal
coordinates $k[[x_1,\ldots,x_d]]$ in that same field/characteristic domain.
The actual ring inclusion is assumed finite; it is not required to arise
from a group action, be flat or admit an algebraization of its formal map.
Then EVERY continuous finite signed obstacle on EVERY full primary
section of R has a continuous greatest independently geometric C/D
minorant. Formula (7), exact contraction (8), every-degree uniform
canonical convergence, and the all-support model rate (11) hold.
For a finite signed REAL linear combination of primary/unit ideal
profiles the rate constant is $n(K_0+M_1)$, with $K_0$ from the source
proof below. No general continuous-obstacle rate or finite generation
is claimed. This theorem requires a supplied actual cover; it does not
produce one for arbitrary normal germs or identify its target as a
finite-group quotient.

We reconstruct source continuity here, rather than accepting 430 n1
as a support or repeating it as a new result. Its six complete immediate
BFJ carriers were physically read for this application: setting and
simple modifications, 1.10--1.15, 2.1--2.8, 3.1--3.14, and 3.15--3.25,
including the complete 3.18 and 3.9--3.10 proofs. Literal bodies remain
LOCALONLY. The following proof uses ENTIRE G331's exact BFJ comparison;
its model, full-support, source and historical-audit qualifications are

centre of dimension at least two. A signed primary model function F is

barrier lies below F, finite maxima direct the family of nef minorants,

using multiplier ideals and bounded thinness. Interior convex continuity
alone is not sufficient and is not substituted.

\]
over ALL simple retractions. On any refinement of the fixed complex,
